morning.description: Wake up with the sun. Drink a glass of warm water with a pinch of rock salt and a squeeze of lemon to stimulate sluggish digestion.
Gentle, warming yoga and Nadi Shodhana (Alternate Nostril Breathing). Followed by Abhyanga (warm oil massage) with sesame oil.
Warm, cooked breakfast like oatmeal or stewed apples. Avoid cold, dry, or raw foods.

afternoon.description: Main meal of the day. Warm, moist, and grounding foods with healthy fats.
Engage in creative or focused work. Sip warm herbal teas (ginger, cumin, fennel) to stay hydrated.

evening.description: Gentle walk or restorative stretching to transition from work to rest.
Warm, easy-to-digest meal like kitchari or soups. Keep portions moderate.

night.description: Digital sunset. Warm milk with nutmeg and ashwagandha. Massage feet with warm oil.
Aim to be in bed by 10 PM for deep, restorative sleep.

morning.description: Wake up slightly before sunrise. Drink room temperature water with mint or lime.
Moderate exercise, cooling yoga, and Sheetali Pranayama. Occasional coconut oil massage.
Substantial but cooling breakfast, like porridge or sweet, ripe fruits.

afternoon.description: The largest and most important meal. Include sweet, bitter, and astringent tastes to balance heat.
High-focus work. Take breaks to cool down and avoid overworking.

evening.description: Nature walk or time near water to dissipate the day's accumulated heat.
Moderate dinner. Avoid excessively spicy, sour, or salty foods.

night.description: Read, meditate, or engage in calming activities. Avoid heated discussions or screens.
Lights out by 10:30 PM. Keep the bedroom cool and well-ventilated.

morning.description: Wake up early before sunrise to avoid heaviness. Drink warm water with raw honey and ginger.
Vigorous exercise, heating yoga (Sun Salutations), and Kapalabhati Pranayama. Dry brushing (Garshana).
Very light breakfast, or skip it entirely if not hungry. Fresh fruit or warm spiced tea is ideal.

afternoon.description: Main meal of the day. Focus on warm, light, and spiced foods. Favor bitter, astringent, and pungent tastes.
Stay active and engaged. Avoid afternoon naps which increase Kapha.

evening.description: A brisk walk or light workout to maintain circulation and energy.
The lightest meal of the day. Soups or steamed vegetables with warming spices.

night.description: Engage in stimulating reading or hobbies. Sip herbal tea like ginger or cinnamon.
Retire to bed by 10:30 - 11:00 PM. Requires less sleep than other doshas (about 6-7 hours).

morning.description: Wake near sunrise. Drink warm water to stimulate digestion.
Moderate yoga and balanced pranayama. Oil pulling and light self-massage.
A balanced, nourishing breakfast suitable for the current season.

afternoon.description: The largest meal. A balanced plate with all six tastes.
Engage in daily duties with focus and balanced energy.

evening.description: A moderate, early dinner, lighter than lunch.

night.description: Relaxing activities, moving away from screens. Asleep by 10:00 PM.

Vata: Vrikshasana (Tree Pose) - for grounding and stability.
Balasana (Child's Pose) - to calm the nervous system.
Paschimottanasana (Seated Forward Bend) - for deep relaxation.
Pitta: Bhujangasana (Cobra Pose) - gentle opening, avoiding overheating.
Chandra Namaskar (Moon Salutations) - cooling and calming.
Ardha Matsyendrasana (Half Lord of the Fishes) - aids liver and digestion.
Kapha: Surya Namaskar (Sun Salutations) - vigorous and heating.
Virabhadrasana (Warrior Poses) - for strength and stamina.
Ustrasana (Camel Pose) - opens the chest and invigorates.

Vata: Nadi Shodhana (Alternate Nostril Breathing) - balances left and right brain, calms anxiety.
Ujjayi (Victorious Breath) - warming and deeply grounding.
Pitta: Sheetali (Cooling Breath) - cools the body and mind.
Bhramari (Bee Breath) - soothes frustration and anger.
Kapha: Kapalabhati (Skull Shining Breath) - energizing, heating, and clears stagnation.
Balanced: Nadi Shodhana (Alternate Nostril Breathing) - excellent for overall harmony.

Spring.name: Vasanta (Spring)
guidelines: Increase vigorous exercise to counteract spring lethargy.
Favor pungent, bitter, and astringent tastes.
Avoid heavy, sweet, sour, and excessively oily foods.

Summer.name: Grishma (Summer)
guidelines: Favor cooling, hydrating foods and drinks.
Avoid excessive spicy, sour, or salty foods.
Exercise during the cooler parts of the day (early morning).
Protect yourself from the midday sun.

Autumn.name: Sharad (Autumn)
guidelines: Transition to warmer, grounding, and nourishing foods.
Establish a very consistent daily routine.
Favor sweet, slightly salty, and sour tastes.
Protect against cold winds and dryness.

Winter.name: Hemanta & Shishira (Winter)
guidelines: Eat warm, heavy, and nourishing meals.
Use warming spices like ginger, cinnamon, and cloves.
Maintain regular exercise to keep circulation strong.
Get plenty of rest, as nights are longer.
